question.text: An acquirer makes an open offer where the total consideration is Rs. 600 crore. Applying the SEBI (SAST) escrow scale, what is the minimum escrow amount required?

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook escrow scale is 25% of the consideration on the first Rs. 500 crore, plus 10% of the balance consideration above Rs. 500 crore. For an open offer of Rs. 600 crore: 25% x Rs. 500 crore = Rs. 125 crore, plus 10% x Rs. 100 crore = Rs. 10 crore, giving Rs. 135 crore in total. The Trap: Rs. 150 crore reflects a flat 25% of the whole consideration and ignores the lower 10% rate that applies on the slice above Rs. 500 crore. Rs. 100 crore reflects a non-existent "Rs. 100 crore floor". Note: The tiered escrow scale always produces a smaller number than a flat 25% once the consideration crosses Rs. 500 crore, because the marginal rate drops from 25% to 10%.
